record.paper_title: Minimal positive realizations: a survey of recent results and open problems
record.original_question: How does the minimality problem for positive realizations extend from the single-input single-output case to the multiple-input multiple-output case? In particular, for MIMO positive systems, what are the right conditions and methods for determining the smallest state dimension of a positive realization, given that this extension is not straightforward even though the existence problem behaves more directly in the SISO setting studied in the paper?

evidence.quote: In the following we will restrict ourself to consider only the SISO discrete-time case.
Lastly, we mention the MIMO case, which is not a straightforward extension of the SISO case, as for the existence problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A discrete-time linear time-invariant system with p inputs and q outputs is described by a transfer matrix H(z), an q×p matrix of rational functions of z that are strictly proper (i.e. each entry tends to 0 as z → ∞). A positive realization of H(z) of dimension n is a quadruple (A, B, C, D) with A ∈ R^{n×n}, B ∈ R^{n×p}, C ∈ R^{q×n}, D ∈ R^{q×p} whose entries are all nonnegative, such that

  H(z) = D + C (zI − A)^{-1} B.

The dimension n is called the order of the realization. A positive realization is called minimal if no positive realization of H(z) has strictly smaller order. Denote by n_+(H) the minimal order of a positive realization of H(z), when one exists.

Problem. Develop necessary and sufficient conditions, together with constructive procedures, that determine n_+(H) for an arbitrary q×p strictly proper rational transfer matrix H(z) admitting a positive realization, in the genuinely multi-input multi-output setting (p > 1 or q > 1). In particular:

(a) Characterize n_+(H) in terms of intrinsic data of H(z) (e.g. its poles, residue structure, factorizations, or associated cone-invariance data), going beyond the known lower and upper bounds.

(b) Provide an algorithm that, given H(z) admitting a positive realization, computes a positive realization (A, B, C, D) whose order equals n_+(H).

A complete solution is known to be elusive because the MIMO minimality problem does not reduce in a direct way to the single-input single-output case (where H(z) is scalar), in contrast with the corresponding existence problem.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent surveys and research on minimal positive realizations indicate that, even in the SISO case, no general procedure is known to determine the minimum state dimension of a positive realization, and only lower/upper bounds are available. The MIMO extension is recognized as significantly harder and remains open, with ongoing work providing only partial results (e.g., bounds, special transfer-function classes, Markov-realization variants).

status_evidence.title: Minimal positive realizations: A survey - ScienceDirect
status_evidence.snippet: It is not known, to date, how to determine in general the minimum dimension of a positive realization; only lower and upper bounds are available.
status_evidence.claim: The minimum dimension of a positive realization is not known in general; only bounds are available.

status_evidence.title: An upper bound on the dimension of minimal positive realizations for discrete time systems
status_evidence.snippet: Provides an upper bound on the dimension of minimal positive realizations for discrete-time systems.
status_evidence.claim: Research continues to provide bounds rather than exact characterizations, indicating the problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Minimal positive Markov realizations
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) work investigating minimal positive Markov realizations.
status_evidence.claim: Active recent research on related minimality questions for positive systems, with no general MIMO solution announced.
